claims.text: CSD shows up as tender lymph nodes 1 to 3 weeks after the scratch; usually resolves on its own
claims.quote: Enlarged, tender lymph nodes that develop 1–3 weeks after exposure to a cat ... Most cases of CSD resolve without antibiotic treatment.

claims.text: Enlarged tender nodes 1-3 weeks after exposure, sometimes papule or pustule at the scratch site and low-grade fever; caused by Bartonella henselae
claims.quote: Low-grade fever; Enlarged, tender lymph nodes that develop 1–3 weeks after exposure to a cat; A papule or pustule at the site of the scratch

claims.text: Table: lymph nodes enlarge 1 to 3 weeks after exposure
claims.quote: Enlarged, tender lymph nodes that develop 1–3 weeks after exposure to a cat

claims.text: Bacteria can spread when a scratch, particularly from a kitten, is contaminated with flea feces (replaces former ref 3)
claims.quote: develop CSD when scratched by domestic or feral cats, particularly kittens. ... The bacteria can be transmitted from a cat to a person when the scratch is contaminated with flea feces (poop).

claims.text: Rarely, infection spreads to the eye, liver, spleen, brain, bones or heart valves
claims.quote: Rarely, infections of the eye, liver, spleen, brain, bones, or heart valves can occur.

claims.text: Prevention bullets: avoid scratches/bites/licks esp. kittens and strays; wash hands; clean scratch with soap and water; flea prevention, never permethrin on cats; keep cats indoors
claims.quote: Avoid cat scratches, bites, and licks, especially from kittens or stray cats. ... Wash hands promptly after handling cats. Clean scratch wounds with soap and water.

claims.text: Prevention bullets (continued): flea prevention, no permethrin, indoors
claims.quote: Talk to your veterinarian about flea prevention products for your cat. Never use products that contain permethrin on cats. Keep cats indoors and away from stray cats.

claims.text: Key takeaway: antibiotics 'sometimes recommended' for otherwise healthy patients; severe cases and immunocompromised patients should be treated
claims.quote: Antibiotic treatment of otherwise healthy patients is sometimes recommended depending on patient and provider preference and symptom severity. ... Severe cases and immunocompromised patients should be treated with antibiotics.

claims.text: CDC bullet: usually self-limited but antibiotics may reduce symptom duration; sometimes recommended; severe cases and immunocompromised treated; requires antibiotics if immunocompromised
claims.quote: CSD is usually self-limited but antibiotic treatment may reduce symptom duration. Severe cases and immunocompromised patients should be treated with antibiotics. ... CSD requires antibiotic treatment if the patient is immunocompromised.

claims.text: CDC advises consulting an infectious disease expert about treatment for disseminated disease
claims.quote: Disseminated CSD such as retinitis, peliosis hepatis, and endocarditis, require longer treatment courses ... Consult with an infectious disease expert about treatment options for these presentations.

claims.text: Needle drainage of a node generally not recommended except for severe pain and swelling or unclear diagnosis
claims.quote: lymph node aspiration is not generally recommended except to relieve severe pain and swelling or in cases where the diagnosis is unclear.
